title: Give the sensor its 3 volts
story: A small sensor behaves like a 1 kohm resistor (R1) and wants about 3 V. All you have is a 9 V battery. Put one resistor in series between the battery and the sensor so that the sensor gets between 2.5 and 3.2 V. Going round the loop, the 9 V the battery gives must be shared out between your resistor and the sensor.

goals.label: your resistor drops between 5.8 and 6.5 V

hints: KVL: 9 V = (drop across your resistor) + (drop across the sensor).
If the sensor gets 3 V, your resistor must drop 6 V, twice as much as the sensor.
The same current flows through both, so the resistor that drops twice the voltage has about twice the resistance.
